items.title: McNeal Breaux Interview, 1958-11-24
items.q: I mean, you take, for instance, McClane. I think he's got a soft touch. He's a nice bass player... But he's, he's a fine bass man, but he's a very soft man.

ctx.x: You think most of the New Orleans fellas played pretty heavy, would you say?

Well, no, we have quite a few of them that play soft bass. I mean, you take, for instance, McClane. I think he's got a soft touch. He's a nice bass player, a real nice bass, but he's, he plays a soft bass. I think he's got an amplifier now. An amplifier would help him. I don't think he uses it in the paddock. No. But he's a, he's a fine bass man, but he's a very soft man. Rick Hart plays soft too most of the time. He, he carries an amplifier. Yeah. But I just don't like the, the amplified bass. I don't care too…

What about the laminated wood? You mentioned that once. Do you think that, can you tell the difference between the old style construction, carved out of one big thick piece of wood, they start the big thing four or five inches thick when they make them right?
